# Crawl Authentication Credentials (app layer)

Per-session credentials so the crawler can open protected pages. App-layer only —
the libraries stay auth-agnostic; the crawler receives resolved headers through
`CrawlerConfig.secret_headers`. Modules: `crypto.py`, `credentials.py`, `store.py`
(pure/testable), `auth_ui.py` (Streamlit rendering).

## Constraints

- **Encryption at rest (`crypto.py`).** Secrets are encrypted with `cryptography`'s Fernet. The key is `derive_credential_key(zip_signing_secret, session_id)` = urlsafe-b64 of `sha256("{secret}:{session_id}")`, so each session encrypts under a distinct key and a credential file lifted into another session is undecryptable. This is at-rest protection against exposure through the Output Files preview/download UI — not a guarantee against someone holding the server secret and session id. `CredentialCipher.decrypt` returns `None` (never raises) on a wrong-key/tampered/malformed token.
- **Models (`credentials.py`) are pure Pydantic v2.** `HttpCredential` (Basic/Bearer) declares `SECRET_FIELDS` (the fields the store encrypts); everything else is display metadata. `http_authorization_header` builds `Authorization: Bearer <token>` or `Basic <base64(user:pass)>`. `select_http_credential` / `select_http_secret_headers` pick the **longest** URL-prefix match among stored HTTP credentials (most specific wins), returning `{}` when none match. Keep these functions UI-free and unit-tested.
- **Storage (`store.py`) splits metadata from secrets.** On disk (`<session>/authentication/credentials.json`) each entry keeps `id`/`kind`/`name`/`auth_type`/`created_at` in clear text and one encrypted `payload` blob (JSON of the `SECRET_FIELDS`). `list_credential_rows` reads metadata only (no cipher) so rendering never decrypts; `load_credentials` decrypts (crawl-time), skipping any entry that fails to decrypt or validate. `add_credential` encrypts + appends; `delete_credentials` removes by id(s) without touching other rows' ciphertext. All paths go through `ensure_within_root`. A corrupt/missing file degrades to empty, never raises.
- **Crawl wiring.** `resolve_http_secret_headers(session_root, signing_secret, session_id, urls)` loads + matches HTTP credentials into an `Authorization` header. The shell's `_start_job` calls it and sets `CrawlerConfig.secret_headers` **after** `build_configs`, so auth reaches the browser/document requests but never the form values or run-metadata front matter. One `Authorization` header applies per crawl (browser headers are global).
- **UI (`auth_ui.py`).** `render_authentication_panel(strings, disabled)` renders a collapsed **Authentication** expander (placed **below** the crawl-settings form in `app_pages/crawl4md.py`) with a compact HTTP header — a bold **title** stacked over a dim one-line **subtitle** (`_http_header_html`, rendered via `st.markdown(help=…, unsafe_allow_html=True)` so the hint icon sits beside it) — and two **icon-only** buttons side by side (primary **Add** and **Delete selected**, tooltipped from `AUTH_ADD_BUTTON`/`AUTH_DELETE_SELECTED`), then the stored credentials as an `st.dataframe` (`hide_index`, `selection_mode="multi-row"`, `on_select="rerun"`). **Delete selected** (enabled from the table's persisted selection, read via `_selected_ids` before the dataframe renders) opens the shared `render_confirm_dialog` and calls `store.delete_credentials`. Pure helpers `credential_dataframe_rows` / `selected_credential_ids` build the table and map selections to ids. Add opens an HTTP `@st.dialog` whose type selectbox reactively swaps the token vs `username:password` field (plain widgets, not `st.form`). Add/delete run inline then `st.rerun()`. The list shows **only** metadata — never a decrypted secret; no view/edit (modify = delete + re-add). Disable add/delete while a crawl job is active.
- **Never log or echo secret values** (tokens, passwords, client secrets). Follow logging.instructions.md — INFO/DEBUG lifecycle only, no PII/secret text. Add both EN and ID i18n keys for any new user-facing text (streamlit.instructions.md).
- **Tests** (`test_auth_crypto.py`, `test_auth_credentials.py`, `test_auth_store.py`, `test_auth_ui.py`) cover crypto round-trip + wrong-key failure, header building + prefix matching, encrypted-at-rest round-trip (assert the raw file has no plaintext secret) + delete, and the pure label helper. Use `tmp_path`; never touch a real session root or network. Do not add rendering/label assertions (Streamlit tests policy).
